research_question: Hvordan beveger musikk, mennesker, instrumenter og kategorier seg gjennom maktstrukturer?

bibliographic_identity.title: 'Seeing' Music in Early Twentieth Century Colonial Algeria

production_source_extensions.registration_reason: Publisher-hosted, peer-reviewed open-access study of identified colonial Algerian music postcards. The article gives object-level front/reverse, date, sender, recipient, place, imprint, industrial-circulation and representation evidence for the Oran Promenade de l'Etang concert postcard sent to Metropolitan France in 1906, while explicitly separating photographed representation from sound, repertoire and audience response.

locators.section: Introduction; Music, image, and synaesthesia; French understandings of colonial Algeria
locators.supports: Wilford identifies postcards as an inexpensive communication medium between colonial Algeria and Europe, documents their role as visual substitutes where French publics had little access to Algerian sound, and locates production and reception within French colonial tourism, industry and representational power.

locators.section: 'Western' music in Algerian spaces; The Kiosque du Musique on the postcard
locators.supports: The selected object is identified as an Oran Promenade de l'Etang orchestral-concert postcard sent to Metropolitan France in 1906. Its reverse links Jacques to Madame Rigole in Oms; the front carries the LL imprint. Wilford traces the relevant French printing-house pattern, resale and postmark route while retaining uncertainty about the photographer's identity.

Wilford argues that postcards normalized European music in colonial public space and exoticized Muslim, Amazigh and Jewish musicians for metropolitan viewers. The conclusion treats the cards as evidence of colonial representation and circulation, not transparent records of sound or complete Algerian musical life.

version_and_identity.object_form: Picture postcard with a photographed orchestral concert on the front and a short written New Year greeting, address and postal evidence on the reverse.
version_and_identity.front_identity: Printed title identifies Oran and the Promenade de l'Etang concert; the front bears the initials LL.
version_and_identity.date_and_route: Sent from colonial Algeria to Metropolitan France in 1906.
version_and_identity.sender: Jacques; no further identity established in the reviewed source.
version_and_identity.recipient: Madame Rigole in Oms, a commune in the French Pyrenees; no further identity established in the reviewed source.
version_and_identity.represented_event: An orchestral performance on the bandstand at Promenade de l'Etang, Oran, before an audience that appears predominantly European.
version_and_identity.photographer_or_imprint_status: LL is present on the card. Wilford reports that the photographer was never formally identified and presents Léon et Lévy as a scholarly attribution, not a resolved personal identity.
version_and_identity.production_and_distribution_context: Wilford documents the broader French postcard-industry pattern in which firms photographed Algeria, printed cards in France and sold them back through North African businesses; the exact production journey of this individual card is not independently reconstructed beyond its LL imprint and documented postal route.
version_and_identity.current_collection: Stephen Wilford personal collection as stated in the article.
version_and_identity.representation_problem: The card moved an image of European public concert life from colonial Oran to France. It is evidence of mediated representation and postal circulation, not an audio record, repertoire list or transparent survey of Algerian musical life.

claim_records.statement: Oran-postkortet fra 1906 dokumenterer en konkret, asymmetrisk sirkulasjonskjede for musikalsk representasjon: et fotografert orkesterarrangement ved Promenade de l'Etang i kolonialt Algerie ble gjort til en LL-merket handels- og postvare og sendt av Jacques til Madame Rigole i Oms i Frankrike. Wilfords fulltekststudie plasserer kortet i en fransk industrikjede der koloniale bilder ble produsert, omsatt og forstått som autentiske uttrykk fra kolonien, samtidig som europeisk konsertliv ble normalisert i algerisk offentlig rom. Det som sirkulerte var derfor ikke bare et nøytralt bilde av 'musikk', men en mediert kategori og romorden formet av kolonial produksjons-, distribusjons- og representasjonsmakt. Caset dokumenterer likevel ikke musikken som faktisk lød, repertoaret, mottakerens reaksjon eller at den foreslåtte Léon-et-Lévy-attribusjonen løser fotografens identitet.

object_scope.object_identity: Oran, Promenade de l'Etang: Le Concert, LL-marked picture postcard sent in 1906 from colonial Algeria by Jacques to Madame Rigole in Oms, France
object_scope.sending_link: Photographed concert and postal dispatch in Oran, colonial Algeria, 1906
intermediary_links: French colonial postcard industry and North African resale pattern
object_scope.receiving_link: Madame Rigole in Oms, Metropolitan France
object_scope.category_translation: A situated public concert in colonial Oran became a portable visual claim about normal European musical life in Algeria.
object_scope.power_relation: French industrial, postal and colonial infrastructures controlled framing and circulation; the selected card does not provide an equivalent local Algerian account.
object_scope.evidence_role: object-bounded history of mediated circulation and colonial representation, not proof of sonic content, musical borrowing, audience effect or complete cultural reception

claim_records.uncertainty: The article identifies the card's place, year, message route, LL mark and present personal-collection context, but History Go has not independently inspected the physical card. Jacques and Madame Rigole are not identified beyond the reverse. The photographer was never formally identified. The broader French printing-and-resale pattern is documented, but every production step for this individual card is not independently proven. The image cannot establish exact repertoire, sound, all audience identities, local Algerian interpretation or Madame Rigole's response.
claim_records.prohibited_inference: Do not infer sonic borrowing, musical origin, appropriation or influence from the image; do not treat the photographed scene as a transparent survey of Algerian musical life; do not state that every visible person was European; do not identify LL or the photographer as certainly Léon et Lévy; do not claim that Madame Rigole interpreted the card musically; do not generalize one postcard into a complete account of French colonial Algeria or transnational music circulation.

boundary_records.statement: Oran-postkortet dokumenterer en fotografert og sirkulert representasjon av et orkesterarrangement, men ikke repertoaret, framføringen, lyden eller soniske lån og opprinnelser.
boundary_records.release_effect: Blocks substitution of visual representation for sonic observation, repertoire evidence or influence history.

boundary_records.statement: Adressen, hilsenen og postgangen dokumenterer at kortet beveget seg fra Algerie til Oms i Frankrike, men de dokumenterer ikke hvordan Madame Rigole tolket bildet eller om musikkmotivet påvirket henne.
boundary_records.release_effect: Separates documented circulation from undocumented reception, cognition and causal effect.

boundary_records.statement: LL-merket er synlig på objektet og kan knyttes til en dokumentert industrihistorie, men den gjennomgåtte studien sier at fotografen aldri ble formelt identifisert; Léon-et-Lévy-forbindelsen må derfor beholdes som attribusjonsforslag.
boundary_records.release_effect: Preserves the intermediary evidence while blocking false certainty about photographer, authorship and the card's complete production route.

boundary_records.statement: Ett bevart postkort og én privat samling kan dokumentere en konkret representasjons- og postrute, men kan ikke representere hele algeriske musikkliv, alle koloniale publikummer eller alle muslimske, amazighske, jødiske og europeiske erfaringer.
boundary_records.release_effect: Keeps the claim object- and route-bounded and blocks essentializing population, religion, ethnicity or national culture.

resolved: The publisher-hosted article gives a persistent scholarly identity and Figure 6 locator for the selected postcard.
The front is tied to Oran, Promenade de l'Etang, the concert image and the LL imprint.
The reverse documents the 1906 route from colonial Algeria by Jacques to Madame Rigole in Oms, France.
The reviewed full text documents photographic framing, French industrial mediation, North African resale and trans-Mediterranean postal circulation.
The case separates represented event, media circulation, category translation and later scholarly interpretation.
Inference boundaries block sonic, repertoire, recipient-effect, photographer-identity and population-wide overreach.
The postcard remains external_link_and_metadata_only; no image is redistributed.
direct_object_gate.release_rule: Only the bounded claim that this identified 1906 postcard moved a colonially framed representation of public music from Oran through industrial and postal intermediaries to a named French recipient may drive questions. Preserve all visual-versus-sonic, reception, attribution and representativeness boundaries.

coverage.known_gap: This production does not reconstruct the exact sound or repertoire in Oran, resolve photographer identity, identify sender or recipient beyond the card, independently inspect the physical object, recover local Algerian interpretation, measure reception in France or generalize one postcard to colonial Algeria as a whole. It opens one trans-Mediterranean representation route with explicit colonial-power and archive limits.
